In this paper we develop a number of models for formulating and evaluating exit strategies for evacuating the Louvre museum in Paris, France.
The Louvre is a famous art museum that houses many incredible artworks, including the Mona Lisa.
Emergencies are multi-faceted; some situations require a more cautious approach while others may be straightforward.
Based on these criteria, we focus on potential bottlenecks and congestion during an exit plan.
For an evacuation plan to be robust in unexpected disasters such as ﬁres, earthquakes, terrorist attacks, or armed shooter situations, it must rely on reliable factors.
A number of terms will be used in this paper to refer to salient feature of our model.
Museum-goer, bystanders: people visiting the Louvre that must be evacuated during an emergency.
